answer_1.quote: To investigate the impact of model editing on paragraph-length outputs from LLMs, we design a protocol, Long-form Evaluation of Model Editing (LEME), for evaluating generations after a model has been edited.
answer_1.outputs: Paragraph‑length passages generated from subject and related prompts

answer_2.quote: We develop the following measures designed to align with the short-form evaluations: (1) Edit consistency, (2) Factual consistency, (3) Internal consistency, (4) Topicality, (5) Naturalness. We also evaluate with ROUGE, BERTScore, perplexity, n‑gram entropy, and an NLI‑based consistency metric.

answer_3.quote: We trained DeBERTaV3 large to predict the survey ratings and also performed zero‑shot and few‑shot prompting with GPT‑4 and GPT‑3.5 as judges of the generated passages.

answer_4.quote: The survey was distributed online to eight computer science graduate students... The survey used a 7‑point Likert scale consisting of nine questions (edit consistency, factual consistency, internal consistency, cross passage consistency, topicality, naturalness, etc.).
answer_4.guideline: Participants rated generated passages using a 7‑point Likert scale on nine criteria covering consistency, topicality and naturalness.
